trajectory_summary: This is a short re-engagement call on an existing lead who already has solar and had a prior Ion touch. The rep re-verifies system ownership, confirms the customer still wants to talk battery, and secures a same-day callback window from a specialist rather than a vague future slot. The call is efficient but thin on orphaned-flow diligence and closes on a soft handshake rather than a locked time.
outcome_dispute: v1 tag is unknown/unlabeled per metadata, so there is nothing to formally dispute, but the observed outcome should be read as a callback (specialist to call within the hour/1-2 hours) rather than a booked appointment — no specific clock time was locked, only a window ('between, like, four and five').

observed_outcome.quote: He can actually give you a call here within the next, hour or two.
observed_outcome.reasoning: No specific day/time was locked — the customer is told a specialist will call within a window (later narrowed to 'between four and five'), which is a callback promise rather than a booked or tentative appointment with a fixed slot.

primary_coaching_focus.why: The call ends on a floating window rather than a committed time and explicit handshake, which is the structural driver of no-shows/missed connects — especially risky here since the customer already flagged he's 'in the plant' and may not hear the phone.

key_moments.quote: Yes. I already have solar. You already have solar?
key_moments.stewart_read: This is the orphaned_flow trigger point — customer confirms existing solar system. The rep correctly pivots into ownership/loan-vs-lease/panel-company questions right after, which is the schema-correct start of the orphaned flow.

key_moments.quote: We just need to see your Who are you? Who what company are you?
key_moments.stewart_read: The customer has to stop the verify flow to ask who's calling — the rep's opening at 00:03 ('Hey. This is Randy.') never stated the company, so legitimacy wasn't established until the customer forced it a minute in.

Rep gets the panel company but the orphaned_flow schema also requires panel size in watts and whether the system is currently working — neither was asked. The 'is your system working' question is a hard_dq trigger if answered negatively, so skipping it leaves a qualification gap.

key_moments.quote: I don't remember who it was. I thought I talked to somebody. But I have some additional questions
key_moments.stewart_read: Customer flags he has 'additional questions' left over from a prior contact, but the rep never asks what those questions are — that content would be immediately useful for the specialist's callback and for the handoff brief.
